name: Linear Optimization
syllabus_body:
ISE 3200 introduces linear optimization: how to model decisions as linear programs, solve them graphically and with the simplex method, and interpret the answers through duality and sensitivity analysis.

Meetings: Mon/Wed 10:20–11:40, Hitchcock Hall 031. Office hours: Tue 2–4 pm, Baker Systems 280.

Learning Objectives

By the end of the course you will be able to:

  1. LO1 — Formulate linear programs from word problems by defining decision variables, an objective and constraints.
  2. LO2 — Convert any LP to standard form using slack and surplus variables, non-negativity and free-variable substitution.
  3. LO3 — Solve two-variable LPs graphically and interpret corner points, unboundedness and multiple optima.
  4. LO4 — Carry out the simplex method: choose entering and leaving variables, perform pivots and recognise optimality, degeneracy and unboundedness.
  5. LO5 — Formulate the dual of an LP and apply weak duality, strong duality and complementary slackness.
  6. LO6 — Interpret shadow prices, reduced costs and the ranges over which the optimal basis stays optimal.
